collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 19 sovereign-state members of the G20 with their nominal GDP (USD millions, 2026), total population (2026), official or national language(s), and government type. The row set is what the cited Wikipedia G20 article reports as sovereign-state members at the 2026-04-30 snapshot; per-row attributes for Government and Official language come from each country's main Wikipedia article infobox at the same snapshot. The two non-state G20 members (the European Union and the African Union) are excluded by construction because the seed asks for 'G20 countries' and the per-row attributes do not apply cleanly to multilateral organizations.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (G20 article): universe + value (defines the 19-row sovereign-state universe; supplies the GDP and Population columns from the article's economic table, anchored to 2026 figures)
- source_urls[1..19] (per-country Wikipedia articles, alphabetical by country): entity-detail + value (each per-country article's first infobox supplies that country's Official language(s) and Government type cells; one article per row, exactly the 19 sovereign G20 members)

No separate validation source. Cross-checked the 19-member roster against the G20 article's lead and the Wikipedia 'List of G20 countries' redirect — 19 sovereign states + EU + AU is consistent. The European Union joined in 1999 and the African Union joined at the 2023 G20 Delhi summit; both are non-state members and are recorded only in the temporal_note as scope-exclusions.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass with adaptation. Universe (19 sovereign G20 members) is source-defined; ranking rule does not apply (the CSV is alphabetized by Country); table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff because the G20 roster is widely-known and per-cell GDP/Population/Language/Government attributes are well-documented; row count (19) is comfortably above the gate; confidence gradient is real (Country/Language are very memorable, GDP magnitudes are knowable to within an order of magnitude, Government-type wording is the most calibration-relevant cell because reasonable LLMs may produce semantically-equivalent but differently-worded forms like 'parliamentary democracy' vs. 'parliamentary republic').
- Seed/provenance: seed #14 from example_questions.txt ('List all G20 countries with their approximate GDP in trillions USD, total population, official language, and government type'), with two adaptations: GDP is reported in USD millions for 2026 to match the cited source's precision, and the EU and AU are excluded as non-state members.
- Category: multi_attribute_projection (gap 4) primary; no secondary. The 4-non-key-attribute calibration test is exactly the multi_attribute_projection use case.
- Source plan: hybrid Tier B Wikipedia (G20 article for GDP/Population, per-country articles for Government and Official language); gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 20.
- Expected shape: 19 rows x 5 columns; PK = Country.
- Domain: Business/Economics (mild overlap; previously 1 instance).
- Risks/adaptation: source_count=20 is high; this is the cost of taking each Government/Language cell from a clean per-country canonical source rather than from Wikidata (which has unfixable data-quality issues at multiple cells; see the SPARQL probe rejection below).
- Decision: Stage.

Seed adaptations:
1. GDP unit normalized from 'approximate trillions USD' (seed wording) to 'USD millions, 2026' (cited source's unit and year). The conversion is documented and the column header makes the unit explicit.
2. European Union and African Union excluded. The seed says 'G20 countries' and Government type / Official language do not apply cleanly to multilateral organizations (EU has 24 official languages, AU has 6, and neither has a single 'government type' in the country sense).

Wikidata SPARQL (Tier A) was attempted first per the picker-guide recommendation and rejected as the source plan after a probe surfaced unfixable per-cell data-quality issues: (a) the United States Q30 lists 'Hawaiian, Spanish' as P37 (official language) — a Wikidata data error that does not match the country's actual de facto English nor the 2025 Executive-Order designation, (b) Russia Q159 lists 36 P37 values covering the official languages of every constituent republic (Abaza, Adyghe, Aghul, Avar, Azerbaijani, Bashkir, ...) which is technically true at the republic level but not at the federal level, (c) P122 (basic form of government) returns 3-7 multi-value entries per country including contested labels (China gets 'communist dictatorship', South Africa formerly returned 'apartheid' until end-time filtering removed it, Mexico formerly returned 'empire' for the same reason) and historical entries, and (d) the per-cell calibration test for multi_attribute_projection is undermined when the source itself is ambiguous about which value is canonical. Switching to Tier B per-country Wikipedia infoboxes resolves all four issues at the cost of source_count=20. The Tier A vs. Tier B trade-off is recorded here so a future v2 can revisit if Wikidata's curation improves on the four offending properties.

Category <-> operation_type pairing: query_category=multi_attribute_projection pairs canonically with operation_type=projection per references/artifact-contract.md. The 4-attribute SELECT is the canonical projection structure.

Post-audit (2026-04-30): two BLOCKING factual fixes applied to the South Africa row, plus one consistency fix to the Russia row. (a) South Africa Official language(s) extended from 11 to 12 entries (added South African Sign Language, which became South Africa's 12th official language in 2023) and re-labelled to the source's own forms (Sepedi / Sesotho / Setswana / Tshivenda / Xitsonga rather than the alternate short forms Pedi / Sotho / Tswana / Venda / Tsonga that prior staging used). (b) South Africa Government type extended from 'Unitary parliamentary republic' to 'Unitary parliamentary republic with an executive presidency' to match the cited South_Africa Wikipedia infobox verbatim. (c) Russia Government type restored from the prior trimmed 'Federal semi-presidential republic' to the full source phrase 'Federal semi-presidential republic under an authoritarian dictatorship' for consistency with the audit's verbatim-infobox policy applied to South Africa; the prior 'curator-judgment trim' rule has been retired and the same source-defined verbatim policy now applies to all 19 rows.
normalization_decisions:
GDP: extracted as integer USD millions from the G20 article's 'Nom. GDP mil. USD (2026)' column with separator commas removed. The seed asked for 'approximate trillions USD' but the cited source's precision is millions and pinning to millions is more honest than fabricating a trillion-rounded value. Population: extracted as integer from the G20 article's 'Population (2026)' column with separator commas removed. Country names: the G20 article uses 'Saudi Arabia', 'South Africa', 'South Korea', 'United Kingdom', 'United States' (space-separated, no underscores) and the staged CSV preserves this convention even though the per-country Wikipedia URLs use underscores. Official language(s): values are verbatim from each country's first infobox 'Official language(s)' or 'National language' field after stripping footnote markers ([1], [a], [c]), CSS class blobs from .mw-parser-output expansion, and normalizing
separators to '; '. Four countries (Argentina, Australia, Japan, United Kingdom) use the 'National language' infobox label rather than 'Official language(s)' because they have no statutory de jure federal official language and their Wikipedia infoboxes report only the de facto national language; the column header is 'Official language(s)' across the table and the four de facto values are documented in temporal_note and _extraction_notes. China's Standard Chinese cell is reported with the '(de facto)' qualifier verbatim from the source page. South Korea's value is preserved as 'Korean; Korean Sign Language' from the infobox. South Africa's 12-language list could not be auto-extracted because the South Africa Wikipedia infobox uses a multi-section structure with one section per language; the staged value 'Afrikaans; English; Ndebele; Sepedi; Sesotho; Setswana; South African Sign Language; Swazi; Tshivenda; Xhosa; Xitsonga; Zulu' (semicolon-delimited, alphabetical) was hand-assembled from the cited South_Africa Wikipedia article's infobox using the source's own label forms (post-audit fix: prior staging used the alternate short labels Pedi/Sotho/Tsonga/Venda and dropped South African Sign Language, which became the 12th official language in 2023; the audit corrected both omissions). Government type: values are verbatim from each country's first infobox 'Government' field after stripping footnote markers, and the verbatim policy is now applied consistently across all 19 rows (post-audit fix: prior staging trimmed Russia's 'under an authoritarian dictatorship' qualifier to the canonical first phrase, but the audit's source-defined verbatim policy was applied consistently — both Russia's full 'Federal semi-presidential republic under an authoritarian dictatorship' and South Africa's full 'Unitary parliamentary republic with an executive presidency' are preserved as cited, with no curator-judgment trims).
open_questions: 1. Whether GDP should be reported in trillions (matching the seed's wording but losing precision) or millions (matching the source). Current design uses millions. 2. Whether the European Union and African Union should be added as separate rows with sentinel values for the Government/Language cells, accepting a wider claim_type. Current design excludes them as scope. 3. Whether the per-country Wikipedia URLs are the right entity-detail source or whether each cell should be cross-referenced to the corresponding Wikidata QID page; current design uses Wikipedia for stable English-prose phrasing of values like 'Federal presidential republic' that Wikidata does not encode as a single string.
